items.text:
pname:magFilter is a elink:VkFilter value specifying the magnification
filter to apply to lookups.

items.name: minFilter
items.text:
pname:minFilter is a elink:VkFilter value specifying the minification
filter to apply to lookups.

items.name: mipmapMode
items.text:
pname:mipmapMode is a elink:VkSamplerMipmapMode value specifying the
mipmap filter to apply to lookups.

items.name: addressModeU
items.text:
pname:addressModeU is a elink:VkSamplerAddressMode value specifying the
<<textures-wrapping-operation,wrapping operation>> used when the [eq]#i#
coordinate used to sample the image would be out of bounds.

items.name: addressModeV
items.text:
pname:addressModeV is a elink:VkSamplerAddressMode value specifying the
<<textures-wrapping-operation,wrapping operation>> used when the [eq]#j#
coordinate used to sample the image would be out of bounds.

items.name: addressModeW
items.text:
pname:addressModeW is a elink:VkSamplerAddressMode value specifying the
<<textures-wrapping-operation,wrapping operation>> used when the [eq]#k#
coordinate used to sample the image would be out of bounds.
If pname:unnormalizedCoordinates is ename:VK_TRUE, pname:addressModeW is
ignored.

items.name: mipLodBias
items.text:
pname:mipLodBias is the bias to be added to
mipmap LOD calculation and bias provided by image sampling functions in
SPIR-V, as described in the <<textures-level-of-detail-operation, LOD
Operation>> section.

items.name: anisotropyEnable
items.text:
pname:anisotropyEnable is ename:VK_TRUE to
enable anisotropic filtering, as described in the
<<textures-texel-anisotropic-filtering, Texel Anisotropic Filtering>>
section, or ename:VK_FALSE otherwise.

items.name: maxAnisotropy
items.text:
pname:maxAnisotropy is the anisotropy value clamp used by the sampler
when pname:anisotropyEnable is ename:VK_TRUE.
If pname:anisotropyEnable is ename:VK_FALSE, pname:maxAnisotropy is
ignored.

items.name: compareEnable
items.text:
pname:compareEnable is ename:VK_TRUE to enable comparison against a
reference value during lookups, or ename:VK_FALSE otherwise.
** Note: Some implementations will default to shader state if this member
does not match.

items.name: compareOp
items.text:
pname:compareOp is a elink:VkCompareOp value specifying the comparison
operator to apply to fetched data before filtering as described in the
<<textures-depth-compare-operation, Depth Compare Operation>> section.

items.name: minLod
items.text:
pname:minLod is used to clamp the <<textures-level-of-detail-operation,
minimum of the computed LOD value>>.

items.name: maxLod
items.text:
pname:maxLod is used to clamp the <<textures-level-of-detail-operation,
maximum of the computed LOD value>>.
To avoid clamping the maximum value, set pname:maxLod to the constant
ename:VK_LOD_CLAMP_NONE.

items.name: borderColor
items.text:
pname:borderColor is a elink:VkBorderColor value specifying the
predefined border color to use.

items.name: unnormalizedCoordinates
items.text:
pname:unnormalizedCoordinates
controls whether to use unnormalized or normalized texel coordinates to
address texels of the image.
When pname:unnormalizedCoordinates is ename:VK_TRUE, the range of the
image coordinates used to lookup the texel is in the range of zero to
the image size in each dimension.
When pname:unnormalizedCoordinates is ename:VK_FALSE, the range of image
coordinates is zero to one.
+
When pname:unnormalizedCoordinates is ename:VK_TRUE, images the sampler is
used with in the shader have the following requirements:
+
** The pname:viewType must: be either ename:VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_1D or
ename:VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D.
** The image view must: have a single layer and a single mip level.
+
When pname:unnormalizedCoordinates is ename:VK_TRUE, image built-in
functions in the shader that use the sampler have the following
requirements:
+
** The functions must: not use projection.
** The functions must: not use offsets.

items.text:
ename:VK_SEMAPHORE_TYPE_BINARY specifies a _binary semaphore_ type that
has a boolean payload indicating whether the semaphore is currently
signaled or unsignaled.
When created, the semaphore is in the unsignaled state.

items.name: VK_SEMAPHORE_TYPE_TIMELINE
items.text:
ename:VK_SEMAPHORE_TYPE_TIMELINE specifies a _timeline semaphore_ type
that has a strictly increasing 64-bit unsigned integer payload
indicating whether the semaphore is signaled with respect to a
particular reference value.
When created, the semaphore payload has the value given by the
pname:initialValue field of slink:VkSemaphoreTypeCreateInfo.

items.name: VK_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_ANY_BIT
items.text:
ename:VK_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_ANY_BIT specifies that the semaphore wait
condition is that at least one of the semaphores in
sname:VkSemaphoreWaitInfo::pname:pSemaphores has reached the value
specified by the corresponding element of
sname:VkSemaphoreWaitInfo::pname:pValues.
If ename:VK_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_ANY_BIT is not set, the semaphore wait
condition is that all of the semaphores in
sname:VkSemaphoreWaitInfo::pname:pSemaphores have reached the value
specified by the corresponding element of
sname:VkSemaphoreWaitInfo::pname:pValues.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_LINK_STAGE_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_LINK_STAGE_BIT_EXT specifies that a shader is
linked to all other shaders created in the same flink:vkCreateShadersEXT
call whose slink:VkShaderCreateInfoEXT structures' pname:flags include
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_LINK_STAGE_BIT_EXT.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_ALLOW_VARYING_SUBGROUP_SIZE_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_ALLOW_VARYING_SUBGROUP_SIZE_BIT_EXT specifies
that the <<interfaces-builtin-variables-sgs, code:SubgroupSize>> may:
vary in a
task, mesh, or
compute shader.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_REQUIRE_FULL_SUBGROUPS_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_REQUIRE_FULL_SUBGROUPS_BIT_EXT specifies that the
subgroup sizes must: be launched with all invocations active in a
task, mesh, or
compute shader.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_NO_TASK_SHADER_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_NO_TASK_SHADER_BIT_EXT specifies that a mesh
shader must: only be used without a task shader.
Otherwise, the mesh shader must: only be used with a task shader.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_DISPATCH_BASE_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_DISPATCH_BASE_BIT_EXT specifies that a compute
shader can: be used with flink:vkCmdDispatchBase with a non-zero base
workgroup.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_FRAGMENT_SHADING_RATE_ATTACHMENT_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_FRAGMENT_SHADING_RATE_ATTACHMENT_BIT_EXT
specifies that a fragment shader can: be used with a fragment shading
rate attachment.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_FRAGMENT_DENSITY_MAP_ATTACHMENT_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_FRAGMENT_DENSITY_MAP_ATTACHMENT_BIT_EXT specifies
that a fragment shader can: be used with a fragment density map
attachment.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_INDIRECT_BINDABLE_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_INDIRECT_BINDABLE_BIT_EXT specifies that the
shader can: be used in combination with <<device-generated-commands>>.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_OPACITY_MICROMAP_DISALLOW_MIXED_SPECIAL_INDEX_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_OPACITY_MICROMAP_DISALLOW_MIXED_SPECIAL_INDEX_BIT_EXT
specifies that shader objects cannot: be used with acceleration
structures which are built with geometry that have an index buffer
including both special indices and indices pointing to an associated
micromap array.
Geometry which has an index buffer using only special indices without an
associated micromap array can: be used with this flag.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_INDEPENDENT_SETS_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_INDEPENDENT_SETS_BIT_KHR specifies that
implementations must: ensure that the properties and/or absence of a
particular descriptor set do not influence any other descriptor sets for
the shader.
This allows shader objects to be created with a subset of the total
descriptor sets.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_64_BIT_INDEXING_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_64_BIT_INDEXING_BIT_EXT specifies that the shader
enables <<spirvenv-64bindexing, 64-bit indexing>>.

items.name: VK_SHADER_CREATE_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_BIT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SHADER_CREATE_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_BIT_EXT specifies that the shader
will use descriptor heap mappings instead of descriptor set layouts.

pages.desc: Bitmask specifying additional information about a sparse image resource

items.name: VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_SINGLE_MIPTAIL_BIT
items.text:
ename:VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_SINGLE_MIPTAIL_BIT specifies that the image
uses a single mip tail region for all array layers.

items.name: VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_ALIGNED_MIP_SIZE_BIT
items.text:
ename:VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_ALIGNED_MIP_SIZE_BIT specifies that the
first mip level whose dimensions are not integer multiples of the
corresponding dimensions of the sparse image block begins the mip tail
region.

items.name: VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_NONSTANDARD_BLOCK_SIZE_BIT
items.text:
ename:VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_NONSTANDARD_BLOCK_SIZE_BIT specifies that
the image uses non-standard sparse image block dimensions, and the
pname:imageGranularity values do not match the standard sparse image
block dimensions for the given format.

image block in texels.

pages.desc: Structure specifying sparse image memory bind

items.name: subresource
items.text:
pname:subresource is the image _aspect_ and region of interest in the
image.

items.name: offset
items.text:
pname:offset are the coordinates of the first texel within the image
subresource to bind.

items.name: extent
items.text:
pname:extent is the size in texels of the region within the image
subresource to bind.
The extent must: be a multiple of the sparse image block dimensions,
except when binding sparse image blocks along the edge of an image
subresource it can: instead be such that any coordinate of
[eq]#pname:offset {plus} pname:extent# equals the corresponding
dimensions of the image subresource.

items.name: memory
items.text:
pname:memory is the slink:VkDeviceMemory object that the sparse image
blocks of the image are bound to.
If pname:memory is dlink:VK_NULL_HANDLE, the sparse image blocks are
unbound.

items.name: memoryOffset
items.text:
pname:memoryOffset is an offset into slink:VkDeviceMemory object.
If pname:memory is dlink:VK_NULL_HANDLE, this value is ignored.

items.name: flags
items.text: pname:flags are sparse memory binding flags.

structures in pname:pBinds array

structures

pages.desc: Structure specifying sparse image memory requirements

items.name: formatProperties
items.text:
pname:formatProperties is a slink:VkSparseImageFormatProperties
structure specifying properties of the image format.

items.name: imageMipTailFirstLod
items.text:
pname:imageMipTailFirstLod is the first mip level at which image
subresources are included in the mip tail region.

items.name: imageMipTailSize
items.text:
pname:imageMipTailSize is the memory size (in bytes) of the mip tail
region.
If pname:formatProperties.flags contains
ename:VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_SINGLE_MIPTAIL_BIT, this is the size of the
whole mip tail, otherwise this is the size of the mip tail of a single
array layer.
This value is guaranteed to be a multiple of the sparse block size in
bytes.

items.name: imageMipTailOffset
items.text:
pname:imageMipTailOffset is the opaque memory offset used with
slink:VkSparseImageOpaqueMemoryBindInfo to bind the mip tail region(s).

items.name: imageMipTailStride
items.text:
pname:imageMipTailStride is the offset stride between each array-layer's
mip tail, if pname:formatProperties.flags does not contain
ename:VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_SINGLE_MIPTAIL_BIT (otherwise the value is
undefined:).

items.name: VK_SPIRV_RESOURCE_TYPE_READ_ONLY_STORAGE_BUFFER_BIT_EXT

items.name: VK_SPIRV_RESOURCE_TYPE_READ_WRITE_STORAGE_BUFFER_BIT_EXT

pages.desc: Bitmask specifying sets of stencil state for which to update the compare mask

items.name: VK_STENCIL_FACE_FRONT_BIT
items.text:
ename:VK_STENCIL_FACE_FRONT_BIT specifies that only the front set of
stencil state is updated.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_FACE_BACK_BIT
items.text:
ename:VK_STENCIL_FACE_BACK_BIT specifies that only the back set of
stencil state is updated.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_FACE_FRONT_AND_BACK
items.text:
ename:VK_STENCIL_FACE_FRONT_AND_BACK is the combination of
ename:VK_STENCIL_FACE_FRONT_BIT and ename:VK_STENCIL_FACE_BACK_BIT, and
specifies that both sets of stencil state are updated.

pages.name: VkStencilFaceFlags

pages.desc: Stencil comparison function

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_KEEP
items.text: ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_KEEP keeps the current value.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_ZERO
items.text: ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_ZERO sets the value to 0.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_REPLACE
items.text: ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_REPLACE sets the value to pname:reference.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_INCREMENT_AND_CLAMP
items.text:
ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_INCREMENT_AND_CLAMP increments the current value and
clamps to the maximum representable unsigned value.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_DECREMENT_AND_CLAMP
items.text:
ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_DECREMENT_AND_CLAMP decrements the current value and
clamps to 0.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_INVERT
items.text: ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_INVERT bitwise-inverts the current value.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_INCREMENT_AND_WRAP
items.text:
ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_INCREMENT_AND_WRAP increments the current value and
wraps to 0 when the maximum value would have been exceeded.

items.name: VK_STENCIL_OP_DECREMENT_AND_WRAP
items.text:
ename:VK_STENCIL_OP_DECREMENT_AND_WRAP decrements the current value and
wraps to the maximum possible value when the value would go below 0.

pages.name: VkStencilOp

pages.desc: Structure specifying stencil operation state

items.name: failOp
items.text:
pname:failOp is a elink:VkStencilOp value specifying the action
performed on samples that fail the stencil test.

items.name: passOp
items.text:
pname:passOp is a elink:VkStencilOp value specifying the action
performed on samples that pass both the depth and stencil tests.

items.name: depthFailOp
items.text:
pname:depthFailOp is a elink:VkStencilOp value specifying the action
performed on samples that pass the stencil test and fail the depth test.

items.name: compareOp
items.text:
pname:compareOp is a elink:VkCompareOp value specifying the comparison
operator used in the stencil test.

items.name: compareMask
items.text:
pname:compareMask selects the bits of the unsigned integer stencil
values participating in the stencil test.

items.name: writeMask
items.text:
pname:writeMask selects the bits of the unsigned integer stencil values
updated by the stencil test in the stencil framebuffer attachment.

items.name: reference
items.text:
pname:reference is an integer stencil reference value that is used in
the unsigned stencil comparison.

items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_DESCRIPTION_PER_VIEW_ATTRIBUTES_BIT_NVX specifies that
shaders compiled for this subpass write the attributes for all views in
a single invocation of each
<<pipelines-graphics-subsets-pre-rasterization,pre-rasterization shader
stage>>.
All pipelines compiled against a subpass that includes this bit must:
write per-view attributes to the `*PerViewNV[]` shader outputs, in
addition to the non-per-view (e.g. code:Position) outputs.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_DESCRIPTION_PER_VIEW_POSITION_X_ONLY_BIT_NVX
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_DESCRIPTION_PER_VIEW_POSITION_X_ONLY_BIT_NVX specifies
that shaders compiled for this subpass use per-view positions which only
differ in value in the x component.
Per-view viewport mask can: also be used.

ename:VK_SUBPASS_DESCRIPTION_FRAGMENT_REGION_BIT_EXT specifies that the
framebuffer region is the fragment region, that is, the minimum region
dependencies are by pixel rather than by sample, such that any fragment
shader invocation can: access any sample associated with that fragment
shader invocation.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_DISALLOWED_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_DISALLOWED_EXT specifies that the subpass
is not merged because merging was disabled using
slink:VkRenderPassCreationControlEXT.
If the render pass does not allow subpass merging, then all subpass
statuses are set to this value.
If a subpass description does not allow subpass merging, then only that
subpass's status is set to this value.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_SIDE_EFFECTS_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_SIDE_EFFECTS_EXT specifies that
the subpass is not merged because it contains side effects.

items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_SAMPLES_MISMATCH_EXT specifies
that the subpass is not merged because sample count is not compatible
with the previous subpass.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_VIEWS_MISMATCH_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_VIEWS_MISMATCH_EXT specifies
that the subpass is not merged because view masks do not match with
previous subpass.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_ALIASING_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_ALIASING_EXT specifies that the
subpass is not merged because of attachments aliasing between them.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_DEPENDENCIES_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_DEPENDENCIES_EXT specifies that
the subpass is not merged because subpass dependencies do not allow
merging.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_INCOMPATIBLE_INPUT_ATTACHMENT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_INCOMPATIBLE_INPUT_ATTACHMENT_EXT
specifies that the subpass is not merged because input attachment is not
a color attachment from previous subpass or the formats are
incompatible.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_TOO_MANY_ATTACHMENTS_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_TOO_MANY_ATTACHMENTS_EXT
specifies that the subpass is not merged because of too many
attachments.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE_EXT
specifies that the subpass is not merged because of insufficient memory.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_DEPTH_STENCIL_COUNT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_DEPTH_STENCIL_COUNT_EXT
specifies that the subpass is not merged because of too many
depth/stencil attachments.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_RESOLVE_ATTACHMENT_REUSE_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_RESOLVE_ATTACHMENT_REUSE_EXT
specifies that the subpass is not merged because a resolve attachment is
reused as an input attachment in a subsequent subpass.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_SINGLE_SUBPASS_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_SINGLE_SUBPASS_EXT specifies
that the subpass is not merged because the render pass has only one
subpass.

items.name: VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_UNSPECIFIED_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_SUBPASS_MERGE_STATUS_NOT_MERGED_UNSPECIFIED_EXT specifies that
the subpass is not merged for unspecified reasons.
Implementations should: return this value when no other
ename:VkSubpassMergeStatusEXT value is appropriate.

pages.desc: Structure describing capabilities of a surface

items.name: sType
items.text: pname:sType is a elink:VkStructureType value identifying this structure.

items.name: pNext
items.text:
pname:pNext is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this
structure.

items.name: minImageCount
items.text:
pname:minImageCount is the minimum number of images the specified device
supports for a swapchain created for the surface, and will be at least
one.

items.name: maxImageCount
items.text:
pname:maxImageCount is the maximum number of images the specified device
supports for a swapchain created for the surface, and will be either 0,
or greater than or equal to pname:minImageCount.
A value of 0 means that there is no limit on the number of images,
though there may: be limits related to the total amount of memory used
by presentable images.

items.name: currentExtent
items.text:
pname:currentExtent is the current width and height of the surface, or
the special value [eq]#(0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)# indicating that the
surface size will be determined by the extent of a swapchain targeting
the surface.

items.name: minImageExtent
items.text:
pname:minImageExtent contains the smallest valid swapchain extent for
the surface on the specified device.
The pname:width and pname:height of the extent will each be less than or
equal to the corresponding pname:width and pname:height of
pname:currentExtent, unless pname:currentExtent has the special value
described above.

items.name: maxImageExtent
items.text:
pname:maxImageExtent contains the largest valid swapchain extent for the
surface on the specified device.
The pname:width and pname:height of the extent will each be greater than
or equal to the corresponding pname:width and pname:height of
pname:minImageExtent.
The pname:width and pname:height of the extent will each be greater than
or equal to the corresponding pname:width and pname:height of
pname:currentExtent, unless pname:currentExtent has the special value
described above.

items.name: maxImageArrayLayers
items.text:
pname:maxImageArrayLayers is the maximum number of layers presentable
images can: have for a swapchain created for this device and surface,
and will be at least one.

items.name: supportedTransforms
items.text:
pname:supportedTransforms is a bitmask of
elink:VkSurfaceTransformFlagBitsKHR indicating the presentation
transforms supported for the surface on the specified device.
At least one bit will be set.

items.name: currentTransform
items.text:
pname:currentTransform is elink:VkSurfaceTransformFlagBitsKHR value
indicating the surface's current transform relative to the presentation
engine's natural orientation.

items.name: supportedCompositeAlpha
items.text:
pname:supportedCompositeAlpha is a bitmask of
elink:VkCompositeAlphaFlagBitsKHR, representing the alpha compositing
modes supported by the presentation engine for the surface on the
specified device, and at least one bit will be set.
Opaque composition can: be achieved in any alpha compositing mode by
either using an image format that has no alpha component, or by ensuring
that all pixels in the presentable images have an alpha value of 1.0.

items.name: supportedUsageFlags
items.text:
pname:supportedUsageFlags is a bitmask of elink:VkImageUsageFlagBits
representing the ways the application can: use the presentable images of
a swapchain created
with elink:VkPresentModeKHR set to
ename:VK_PRESENT_MODE_FIFO_LATEST_READY_KHR,
ename:VK_PRESENT_MODE_IMMEDIATE_KHR, ename:VK_PRESENT_MODE_MAILBOX_KHR,
ename:VK_PRESENT_MODE_FIFO_KHR or ename:VK_PRESENT_MODE_FIFO_RELAXED_KHR
for the surface on the specified device.
ename:VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT must: be included in the set.
Implementations may: support additional usages.

items.name: supportedSurfaceCounters
items.text:
pname:supportedSurfaceCounters is a bitmask of
elink:VkSurfaceCounterFlagBitsEXT indicating the supported surface
counter types.
It must: not include ename:VK_SURFACE_COUNTER_VBLANK_BIT_EXT unless the
surface queried is a <<wsi-display-surfaces,display surface>>

items.name: VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_SPLIT_INSTANCE_BIND_REGIONS_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_SPLIT_INSTANCE_BIND_REGIONS_BIT_KHR specifies
that images created from the swapchain (i.e. with the pname:swapchain
member of slink:VkImageSwapchainCreateInfoKHR set to this swapchain's
handle) must: use ename:VK_IMAGE_CREATE_SPLIT_INSTANCE_BIND_REGIONS_BIT.

items.name: VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_PROTECTED_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_PROTECTED_BIT_KHR specifies that images
created from the swapchain are protected images.

items.name: VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_MUTABLE_FORMAT_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_MUTABLE_FORMAT_BIT_KHR specifies that the
images of the swapchain can: be used to create a sname:VkImageView with
a different format than what the swapchain was created with.
The list of allowed image view formats is specified by adding a
slink:VkImageFormatListCreateInfo structure to the pname:pNext chain of
slink:VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR.
In addition, this flag also specifies that the swapchain can: be created
with usage flags that are not supported for the format the swapchain is
created with but are supported for at least one of the allowed image
view formats.

items.name: VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_DEFERRED_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_DEFERRED_MEMORY_ALLOCATION_BIT_KHR specifies
that the implementation may: defer allocation of memory associated with
each swapchain image until its index is to be returned from
flink:vkAcquireNextImageKHR
or flink:vkAcquireNextImage2KHR
for the first time.

applications can: include the sname:VkPresentId2KHR structure in the
pname:pNext chain of the slink:VkPresentInfoKHR structure to associate
an identifier with each presentation request.

items.name: VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_PRESENT_WAIT_2_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_PRESENT_WAIT_2_BIT_KHR specifies that
applications can: use fname:vkWaitForPresent2KHR to wait for the
presentation engine to have begun presentation of the presentation
request associated with slink:VkPresentWait2InfoKHR::pname:presentId on
pname:swapchain.

items.name: VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_MULTISAMPLED_RENDER_TO_SINGLE_SAMPLED_BIT_EXT

ename:VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_MULTISAMPLED_RENDER_TO_SINGLE_SAMPLED_BIT_EXT
specifies that an image can: be used with
<<multisampled-render-to-single-sampled,multisampled rendering as a
single-sampled render pass attachment>>

ename:VK_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_PRESENT_TIMING_BIT_EXT specifies that features
supported by the swapchain device in
slink:VkPhysicalDevicePresentTimingFeaturesEXT can: be used to collect
timing information or schedule presentation requests at specific times.

items.name: sType
items.text: pname:sType is a elink:VkStructureType value identifying this structure.

items.name: pNext
items.text:
pname:pNext is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this
structure.

items.name: flags
items.text:
pname:flags is a bitmask of elink:VkSwapchainCreateFlagBitsKHR
indicating parameters of the swapchain creation.

items.name: surface
items.text:
pname:surface is the surface onto which the swapchain will present
images.
If the creation succeeds, the swapchain becomes associated with
pname:surface.

items.name: minImageCount
items.text:
pname:minImageCount is the minimum number of presentable images that the
application needs.
The implementation will either create the swapchain with at least that
many images, or it will fail to create the swapchain.

items.name: imageFormat
items.text:
pname:imageFormat is a elink:VkFormat value specifying the format the
swapchain image(s) will be created with.

items.name: imageColorSpace
items.text:
pname:imageColorSpace is a elink:VkColorSpaceKHR value specifying the
way the swapchain interprets image data.

items.name: imageExtent
items.text:
pname:imageExtent is the size (in pixels) of the swapchain image(s).
The behavior is platform-dependent if the image extent does not match
the surface's pname:currentExtent as returned by
fname:vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR.
+
[NOTE]
====
On some platforms, it is normal that pname:maxImageExtent may: become `(0,
0)`, for example when the window is minimized.
In such a case, it is not possible to create a swapchain due to the Valid
Usage requirements
, unless scaling is selected through
slink:VkSwapchainPresentScalingCreateInfoKHR, if supported
.
====

items.name: imageArrayLayers
items.text:
pname:imageArrayLayers is the number of views in a multiview/stereo
surface.
For non-stereoscopic-3D applications, this value is 1.

items.name: imageUsage
items.text:
pname:imageUsage is a bitmask of elink:VkImageUsageFlagBits describing
the intended usage of the (acquired) swapchain images.

items.name: imageSharingMode
items.text:
pname:imageSharingMode is the sharing mode used for the image(s) of the
swapchain.

items.name: queueFamilyIndexCount
items.text:
pname:queueFamilyIndexCount is the number of queue families having
access to the image(s) of the swapchain when pname:imageSharingMode is
ename:VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT.

items.name: pQueueFamilyIndices
items.text:
pname:pQueueFamilyIndices is a pointer to an array of queue family
indices having access to the images(s) of the swapchain when
pname:imageSharingMode is ename:VK_SHARING_MODE_CONCURRENT.

items.name: preTransform
items.text:
pname:preTransform is a elink:VkSurfaceTransformFlagBitsKHR value
describing the transform, relative to the presentation engine's natural
orientation, applied to the image content prior to presentation.
If it does not match the pname:currentTransform value returned by
fname:vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceCapabilitiesKHR, the presentation engine
will transform the image content as part of the presentation operation.

items.name: compositeAlpha
items.text:
pname:compositeAlpha is a elink:VkCompositeAlphaFlagBitsKHR value
indicating the alpha compositing mode to use when this surface is
composited together with other surfaces on certain window systems.

items.name: presentMode
items.text:
pname:presentMode is the presentation mode the swapchain will use.
A swapchain's present mode determines how incoming present requests will
be processed and queued internally.

items.name: clipped
items.text:
pname:clipped specifies whether the Vulkan implementation is allowed to
discard rendering operations that affect regions of the surface that are
not visible.
** If pname:clipped is ename:VK_TRUE, the presentable images associated
with the swapchain may: not own all of their pixels.
Pixels in the presentable images that correspond to regions of the
target surface obscured by another window on the desktop, or subject to
some other clipping mechanism will have undefined: content when read
back.
Fragment shaders may: not execute for these pixels, and thus any side
effects they would have had will not occur.
Setting ename:VK_TRUE does not guarantee any clipping will occur, but
allows more efficient presentation methods to be used on some
platforms.
** If pname:clipped is ename:VK_FALSE, presentable images associated with
the swapchain will own all of the pixels they contain.
+
[NOTE]
====
Applications should: set this value to ename:VK_TRUE if they do not expect
to read back the content of presentable images before presenting them or
after reacquiring them, and if their fragment shaders do not have any side
effects that require them to run for all pixels in the presentable image.
====

items.name: oldSwapchain
items.text:
pname:oldSwapchain is dlink:VK_NULL_HANDLE, or the existing non-retired
swapchain currently associated with pname:surface.
Providing a valid pname:oldSwapchain may: aid in the resource reuse, and
also allows the application to still present any images that are already
acquired from it.

pages.desc: Supported time domains

items.name: VK_TIME_DOMAIN_DEVICE_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_TIME_DOMAIN_DEVICE_KHR specifies the device time domain.
Timestamp values in this time domain use the same units and are
comparable with device timestamp values captured using
flink:vkCmdWriteTimestamp
or flink:vkCmdWriteTimestamp2
and are defined to be incrementing according to the
<<limits-timestampPeriod, pname:timestampPeriod>> of the device.

items.name: VK_TIME_DOMAIN_PRESENT_STAGE_LOCAL_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_TIME_DOMAIN_PRESENT_STAGE_LOCAL_EXT specifies a time domain
unique to a particular swapchain and a specific present stage.
Timestamp values in this time domain are in units of nanosecond and are
comparable only with other values from the same swapchain and present
stage.

items.name: VK_TIME_DOMAIN_SWAPCHAIN_LOCAL_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_TIME_DOMAIN_SWAPCHAIN_LOCAL_EXT specifies a time domain unique
to a particular swapchain.
Timestamp values in this time domain are in units of nanosecond and are
comparable only with other values from the same swapchain.

items.name: VK_TIME_DOMAIN_CLOCK_MONOTONIC_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_TIME_DOMAIN_CLOCK_MONOTONIC_KHR specifies the CLOCK_MONOTONIC
time domain available on POSIX platforms.
Timestamp values in this time domain are in units of nanoseconds and are
comparable with platform timestamp values captured using the POSIX
clock_gettime API as computed by this example:

items.name: VK_TIME_DOMAIN_CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_TIME_DOMAIN_CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW_KHR specifies the
CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW time domain available on POSIX platforms.
Timestamp values in this time domain are in units of nanoseconds and are
comparable with platform timestamp values captured using the POSIX
clock_gettime API as computed by this example:

items.name: VK_TIME_DOMAIN_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_COUNTER_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_TIME_DOMAIN_QUERY_PERFORMANCE_COUNTER_KHR specifies the
performance counter (QPC) time domain available on Windows.
Timestamp values in this time domain are in the same units as those
provided by the Windows QueryPerformanceCounter API and are comparable
with platform timestamp values captured using that API as computed by
this example:

pages.desc: Specify validation features to disable

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_ALL_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_ALL_EXT specifies that all
validation checks are disabled.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_SHADERS_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_SHADERS_EXT specifies that shader
validation, both runtime and standalone, is disabled.
This validation occurs inside
slink:VkShaderCreateInfoEXT and
slink:VkShaderModuleCreateInfo.
This feature is enabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_THREAD_SAFETY_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_THREAD_SAFETY_EXT specifies that
thread safety validation is disabled.
This feature is enabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_API_PARAMETERS_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_API_PARAMETERS_EXT specifies that
stateless parameter validation is disabled.
This feature is enabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_OBJECT_LIFETIMES_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_OBJECT_LIFETIMES_EXT specifies that
object lifetime validation is disabled.
This feature is enabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_CORE_CHECKS_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_CORE_CHECKS_EXT specifies that core
validation checks are disabled.
This feature is enabled by default.
If this feature is disabled,
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_SHADERS_EXT is implied.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_UNIQUE_HANDLES_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_UNIQUE_HANDLES_EXT specifies that
protection against duplicate non-dispatchable object handles is
disabled.
This feature is enabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_SHADER_VALIDATION_CACHE_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_DISABLE_SHADER_VALIDATION_CACHE_EXT
specifies that there will be no caching of shader validation results and
every shader will be validated on every application execution.
Shader validation caching is enabled by default.

pages.name: VkValidationFeatureDisableEXT

pages.desc: Specify validation features to enable

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_GPU_ASSISTED_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_GPU_ASSISTED_EXT specifies that
GPU-assisted validation is enabled.
Activating this feature instruments shader programs to generate
additional diagnostic data.
This feature is disabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_GPU_ASSISTED_RESERVE_BINDING_SLOT_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_GPU_ASSISTED_RESERVE_BINDING_SLOT_EXT
specifies that the validation layers reserve a descriptor set binding
slot for their own use.
The layer reports a value for
slink:VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::pname:maxBoundDescriptorSets that is one
less than the value reported by the device.
If the device supports the binding of only one descriptor set, the
validation layer does not perform GPU-assisted validation.
This feature is disabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_BEST_PRACTICES_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_BEST_PRACTICES_EXT specifies that
Vulkan best-practices validation is enabled.
Activating this feature enables the output of warnings related to common
misuse of the API, but which are not explicitly prohibited by the
specification.
This feature is disabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_DEBUG_PRINTF_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_DEBUG_PRINTF_EXT specifies that the
layers will process code:debugPrintfEXT operations in shaders and send
the resulting output to the debug callback.
This feature is disabled by default.

items.name: VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_SYNCHRONIZATION_VALIDATION_EXT
items.text:
ename:VK_VALIDATION_FEATURE_ENABLE_SYNCHRONIZATION_VALIDATION_EXT
specifies that Vulkan synchronization validation is enabled.
This feature reports resource access conflicts due to missing or
incorrect synchronization operations between actions (Draw, Copy,
Dispatch, Blit) reading or writing the same regions of memory.
This feature is disabled by default.

items.name: divisor
items.text:
pname:divisor is the number of successive instances that will use the
same value of the vertex attribute when instanced rendering is enabled.
This member can: be a value other than `1` if the
<<features-vertexAttributeInstanceRateDivisor,
pname:vertexAttributeInstanceRateDivisor>> feature is enabled.
For example, if the divisor is N, the same vertex attribute will be
applied to N successive instances before moving on to the next vertex
attribute.
The maximum value of pname:divisor is implementation-dependent and can
be queried using
sname:VkPhysicalDeviceVertexAttributeDivisorPropertiesEXT::pname:maxVertexAttribDivisor.
A value of `0` can: be used for the divisor if the
<<features-vertexAttributeInstanceRateZeroDivisor,
pname:vertexAttributeInstanceRateZeroDivisor>> feature is enabled.
In this case, the same vertex attribute will be applied to all
instances.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_DECODE_CAPABILITY_DPB_AND_OUTPUT_COINCIDE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_DECODE_CAPABILITY_DPB_AND_OUTPUT_COINCIDE_BIT_KHR
specifies support for using the same video picture resource as the
<<reconstructed-picture,reconstructed picture>> and
<<decode-output-picture,decode output picture>> in a video decode
operation.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_DECODE_CAPABILITY_DPB_AND_OUTPUT_DISTINCT_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_DECODE_CAPABILITY_DPB_AND_OUTPUT_DISTINCT_BIT_KHR
specifies support for using distinct video picture resources as the
<<reconstructed-picture,reconstructed picture>> and
<<decode-output-picture,decode output picture>> in a video decode
operation.
+
[NOTE]
====
Some video profiles allow using distinct video picture resources as the
reconstructed picture and decode output picture in specific video decode
operations even when the video decode profile does not support
ename:VK_VIDEO_DECODE_CAPABILITY_DPB_AND_OUTPUT_DISTINCT_BIT_KHR.
Even if the implementation only reports coincide, the decode output picture
for <<decode-av1-film-grain,film grain>> enabled frames must be a different
video picture resource from the reconstructed picture because film grain is
applied outside of the coding loop.
====

items.name: VK_VIDEO_DECODE_H264_PICTURE_LAYOUT_INTERLACED_INTERLEAVED_LINES_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_DECODE_H264_PICTURE_LAYOUT_INTERLACED_INTERLEAVED_LINES_BIT_KHR
specifies support for or use of a picture layout for interlaced content
where all lines belonging to the top field are decoded to the
even-numbered lines within the picture resource, and all lines belonging
to the bottom field are decoded to the odd-numbered lines within the
picture resource.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_DECODE_H264_PICTURE_LAYOUT_INTERLACED_SEPARATE_PLANES_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_DECODE_H264_PICTURE_LAYOUT_INTERLACED_SEPARATE_PLANES_BIT_KHR
specifies support for or use of a picture layout for interlaced content
where all lines belonging to a field are grouped together in a single
image subregion, and the two fields comprising the frame can: be stored
in separate image subregions of the same image subresource or in
separate image subresources.

items.text:

items.name: codedPictureAlignment
items.text:
pname:codedPictureAlignment indicates the alignment at which the
implementation will code pictures.
This capability does not impose any valid usage constraints on the
application.
However, depending on the pname:codedExtent of the encode input picture
resource, this capability may: result in a change of the resolution of
the encoded picture, as described in more detail below.

items.name: maxTiles
items.text:
pname:maxTiles indicates the maximum number of AV1 tile columns and rows
the implementation supports.

items.name: minTileSize
items.text:
pname:minTileSize indicates the minimum extent of individual AV1 tiles
the implementation supports.

items.name: maxTileSize
items.text:
pname:maxTileSize indicates the maximum extent of individual AV1 tiles
the implementation supports.

items.name: superblockSizes
items.text:

elink:VkVideoEncodeAV1SuperblockSizeFlagBitsKHR values indicating the
supported AV1 superblock sizes.

items.name: maxSingleReferenceCount
items.text:

<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,single reference prediction mode>>.

items.name: singleReferenceNameMask
items.text:

<<encode-av1-reference-names,AV1 reference names>> when using
<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,single reference prediction mode>>.

items.name: maxUnidirectionalCompoundReferenceCount

<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,unidirectional compound prediction mode>>.

maximum number of reference pictures the implementation supports when

items.name: unidirectionalCompoundReferenceNameMask
items.text:
pname:unidirectionalCompoundReferenceNameMask is a bitmask of supported
<<encode-av1-reference-names,AV1 reference names>> when using
<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,unidirectional compound prediction mode>>.

items.name: maxBidirectionalCompoundReferenceCount
items.text:
pname:maxBidirectionalCompoundReferenceCount indicates the maximum
number of reference pictures the implementation supports when using
<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,bidirectional compound prediction mode>>.

items.name: maxBidirectionalCompoundGroup1ReferenceCount
items.text:

<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,bidirectional compound prediction mode>>

items.name: maxBidirectionalCompoundGroup2ReferenceCount

<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,bidirectional compound prediction mode>>

items.name: bidirectionalCompoundReferenceNameMask
items.text:
pname:bidirectionalCompoundReferenceNameMask is a bitmask of supported
<<encode-av1-reference-names,AV1 reference names>> when using
<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,bidirectional compound prediction mode>>.

items.name: maxTemporalLayerCount
items.text:
pname:maxTemporalLayerCount indicates the maximum number of AV1 temporal
layers supported by the implementation.

items.name: maxSpatialLayerCount
items.text:
pname:maxSpatialLayerCount indicates the maximum number of AV1 spatial
layers supported by the implementation.

items.name: maxOperatingPoints
items.text:
pname:maxOperatingPoints indicates the maximum number of AV1 operating
points supported by the implementation.

items.name: minQIndex
items.text: pname:minQIndex indicates the minimum quantizer index value supported.

items.name: maxQIndex
items.text: pname:maxQIndex indicates the maximum quantizer index value supported.

items.name: prefersGopRemainingFrames
items.text:
pname:prefersGopRemainingFrames indicates that the implementation's rate
control algorithm prefers the application to specify the number of
frames in each <<encode-av1-rate-control-group,AV1 rate control group>>
<<encode-av1-gop-remaining-frames,remaining>> in the current
<<encode-av1-gop,group of pictures>> when beginning a
<<video-coding-scope,video coding scope>>.

items.name: requiresGopRemainingFrames
items.text:
pname:requiresGopRemainingFrames indicates that the implementation's
rate control algorithm requires the application to specify the number of
frames in each <<encode-av1-rate-control-group,AV1 rate control group>>
<<encode-av1-gop-remaining-frames,remaining>> in the current
<<encode-av1-gop,group of pictures>> when beginning a
<<video-coding-scope,video coding scope>>.

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeAV1CapabilitiesKHR

pages.desc: AV1 encode capability flags

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_PER_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_MIN_MAX_Q_INDEX_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_PER_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_MIN_MAX_Q_INDEX_BIT_KHR
specifies support for specifying different quantizer index values in the
members of slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1QIndexKHR.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_GENERATE_OBU_EXTENSION_HEADER_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_GENERATE_OBU_EXTENSION_HEADER_BIT_KHR
specifies support for generating OBU extension headers, as defined in
section 5.3.3 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_PRIMARY_REFERENCE_CDF_ONLY_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_PRIMARY_REFERENCE_CDF_ONLY_BIT_KHR
specifies support for using the primary reference frame indicated by the
value of code:StdVideoEncodeAV1PictureInfo::code:primary_ref_frame in
the <<encode-av1-picture-info,AV1 picture information>> only for CDF
data reference, as defined in section 6.8.2 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1
Specification>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_FRAME_SIZE_OVERRIDE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_FRAME_SIZE_OVERRIDE_BIT_KHR
specifies support for encoding a picture with a frame size different
from the maximum frame size defined in the
<<encode-av1-active-sequence-header,active AV1 sequence header>>.
If this capability is not supported, then code:frame_size_override_flag
must: not be set in the <<encode-av1-picture-info,AV1 picture
information>> of the encoded frame and the coded extent of the
<<encode-input-picture,encode input picture>> must: match the maximum
coded extent allowed by the <<encode-av1-active-sequence-header,active
AV1 sequence header>>, i.e. [eq]#(code:max_frame_width_minus_1 {plus} 1,
code:max_frame_height_minus_1 {plus} 1)#.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_MOTION_VECTOR_SCALING_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_MOTION_VECTOR_SCALING_BIT_KHR
specifies support for motion vector scaling, as defined in section
7.11.3.3 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>.
If this capability is not supported, then the coded extent of all
<<active-reference-pictures,active reference pictures>> must: match the
coded extent of the <<encode-input-picture,encode input picture>>.
This capability may: only be supported by a video profile when
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_FRAME_SIZE_OVERRIDE_BIT_KHR is also
supported.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_COMPOUND_PREDICTION_INTRA_REFRESH_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_CAPABILITY_COMPOUND_PREDICTION_INTRA_REFRESH_BIT_KHR
specifies support for encoding frames using
<<encode-av1-prediction-modes,unidirectional or bidirectional compound
prediction mode>> with <<encode-intra-refresh,intra refresh>> enabled.

encoded with
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_PREDICTIVE_KHR.

items.name: bipredictiveFrameSize

pname:bipredictiveFrameSize is the size in bytes to be used for frames
encoded with
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_BIPREDICTIVE_KHR.

items.name: sType

items.name: pNext

structure.

items.name: useGopRemainingFrames
items.text:
pname:useGopRemainingFrames indicates whether the implementation's rate
control algorithm should: use the values specified in
pname:gopRemainingIntra, pname:gopRemainingPredictive, and
pname:gopRemainingBipredictive.
If pname:useGopRemainingFrames is ename:VK_FALSE, then the values of
pname:gopRemainingIntra, pname:gopRemainingPredictive, and
pname:gopRemainingBipredictive are ignored.

items.name: gopRemainingIntra
items.text:
pname:gopRemainingIntra specifies the number of frames encoded with
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_INTRA_KHR the
implementation's rate control algorithm should: assume to be remaining
in the <<encode-av1-gop,GOP>> prior to executing the next video encode
operation.

items.name: gopRemainingPredictive
items.text:
pname:gopRemainingPredictive specifies the number of frames encoded with
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_PREDICTIVE_KHR the
implementation's rate control algorithm should: assume to be remaining
in the <<encode-av1-gop,GOP>> prior to executing the next video encode
operation.

items.name: gopRemainingBipredictive
items.text:
pname:gopRemainingBipredictive specifies the number of frames encoded
with ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_BIPREDICTIVE_KHR the
implementation's rate control algorithm should: assume to be remaining
in the <<encode-av1-gop,GOP>> prior to executing the next video encode
operation.

items.name: sType
items.text: pname:sType is a elink:VkStructureType value identifying this structure.

items.name: pNext

structure.

items.name: predictionMode
items.text:
pname:predictionMode specifies the <<encode-av1-prediction-modes,AV1
prediction mode>> to use for the encoded frame.

items.name: rateControlGroup
items.text:
pname:rateControlGroup specifies the <<encode-av1-rate-control-group,AV1
rate control group>> to use for the encoded frame when the current
<<encode-rate-control-modes,rate control mode>> is not
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_DISABLED_BIT_KHR.
Otherwise it is ignored.

items.name: constantQIndex
items.text:
pname:constantQIndex is the quantizer index to use for the encoded frame
if the current <<encode-rate-control-modes,rate control mode>>
configured for the video session is
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_DISABLED_BIT_KHR.

items.name: pStdPictureInfo
items.text:
pname:pStdPictureInfo is a pointer to a
code:StdVideoEncodeAV1PictureInfo structure specifying
<<encode-av1-picture-info,AV1 picture information>>.

items.name: referenceNameSlotIndices
items.text:
pname:referenceNameSlotIndices is an array of seven
(ename:VK_MAX_VIDEO_AV1_REFERENCES_PER_FRAME_KHR, which is equal to the
Video Std definition code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_REFS_PER_FRAME) signed integer
values specifying the index of the <<dpb-slot, DPB slot>> or a negative
integer value for each <<encode-av1-reference-names,AV1 reference name>>
used for inter coding.
In particular, the DPB slot index for the AV1 reference name code:frame
is specified in pname:referenceNameSlotIndices[code:frame -
code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_REFERENCE_NAME_LAST_FRAME].

items.name: primaryReferenceCdfOnly
items.text:
pname:primaryReferenceCdfOnly controls whether the primary reference
frame indicated by the value of pname:pStdPictureInfo->primary_ref_frame
is used only for CDF data reference, as defined in sections 6.8.2 of the
<<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>.
If set to ename:VK_TRUE, then the primary reference frame's picture data
will not be used for sample prediction.

items.name: generateObuExtensionHeader
items.text:
pname:generateObuExtensionHeader controls whether OBU extension headers
are generated into the target bitstream, as defined in sections 5.3.1,
5.3.2, and 5.3.3 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>.

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeAV1PictureInfoKHR

pages.desc: AV1 encode prediction mode

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_INTRA_ONLY_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_INTRA_ONLY_KHR specifies the
use of _intra-only prediction mode_, used when encoding AV1 frames of
type code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_KEY or
code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_INTRA_ONLY.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_SINGLE_REFERENCE_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_SINGLE_REFERENCE_KHR specifies
the use of _single reference prediction mode_, used when encoding AV1
frames of type code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_INTER or
code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_SWITCH with code:reference_select, as
defined in section 6.8.23 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>,
equal to 0.
When using this prediction mode, the application must: specify a
reference picture for at least one <<encode-av1-reference-names,AV1
reference name>> in
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1PictureInfoKHR::pname:referenceNameSlotIndices
that is supported by the implementation, as reported in
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1CapabilitiesKHR::pname:singleReferenceNameMask.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_UNIDIRECTIONAL_COMPOUND_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_UNIDIRECTIONAL_COMPOUND_KHR
specifies the use of _unidirectional compound prediction mode_, used
when encoding AV1 frames of type code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_INTER or
code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_SWITCH with code:reference_select, as
defined in section 6.8.23 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>,
equal to 1, and both <<encode-av1-reference-names,reference names>> used
for prediction are from the same reference frame group, as defined in
section 6.10.24 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>.
When using this prediction mode, the application must: specify a
reference picture for at least two <<encode-av1-reference-names,AV1
reference names>> in
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1PictureInfoKHR::pname:referenceNameSlotIndices
that is supported by the implementation, as reported in
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1CapabilitiesKHR::pname:unidirectionalCompoundReferenceNameMask,
where those two reference names are one of the allowed pairs of
reference names, as defined in section 5.11.25 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1
Specification>>, listed below:
** code:LAST_FRAME and code:LAST2_FRAME,
** code:LAST_FRAME and code:LAST3_FRAME,
** code:LAST_FRAME and code:GOLDEN_FRAME, or
** code:BWDREF_FRAME and code:ALTREF_FRAME.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_BIDIRECTIONAL_COMPOUND_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_PREDICTION_MODE_BIDIRECTIONAL_COMPOUND_KHR
specifies the use of _bidirectional compound prediction mode_, used when
encoding AV1 frames of type code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_INTER or
code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_SWITCH with code:reference_select, as
defined in section 6.8.23 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>,
equal to 1, and the two <<encode-av1-reference-names,reference names>>
used for prediction are from different reference frame groups, as
defined in section 6.10.24 of the <<aomedia-av1,AV1 Specification>>.
When using this prediction mode, the application must: specify a
reference picture for at least one <<encode-av1-reference-names,AV1
reference name>> from each reference frame group in
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1PictureInfoKHR::pname:referenceNameSlotIndices
that is supported by the implementation, as reported in
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1CapabilitiesKHR::pname:bidirectionalCompoundReferenceNameMask.

GOP structure>> according to the parameters specified in the

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_RATE_CONTROL_TEMPORAL_LAYER_PATTERN_DYADIC_BIT_KHR

when encoding AV1 frames of type code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_KEY or

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeAV1RateControlGroupKHR

pages.desc: Structure describing AV1 stream rate control parameters

items.name: sType
items.text: pname:sType is a elink:VkStructureType value identifying this structure.

items.name: pNext
items.text:
pname:pNext is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this
structure.

items.name: flags
items.text:
pname:flags is a bitmask of elink:VkVideoEncodeAV1RateControlFlagBitsKHR
specifying AV1 rate control flags.

items.name: gopFrameCount
items.text:
pname:gopFrameCount is the number of frames within a <<encode-av1-gop,
group of pictures (GOP)>> intended to be used by the application.
If it is set to 0, the rate control algorithm may: assume an
implementation-dependent GOP length.
If it is set to code:UINT32_MAX, the GOP length is treated as infinite.

items.name: keyFramePeriod
items.text:
pname:keyFramePeriod is the interval, in terms of number of frames,
between two frames with the AV1 frame type
code:STD_VIDEO_AV1_FRAME_TYPE_KEY (see <<encode-av1-key-frame-period,key
frame period>>).
If it is set to 0, the rate control algorithm may: assume an
implementation-dependent key frame period.
If it is set to code:UINT32_MAX, the key frame period is treated as
infinite.

items.name: consecutiveBipredictiveFrameCount
items.text:
pname:consecutiveBipredictiveFrameCount is the number of consecutive
frames encoded with
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_AV1_RATE_CONTROL_GROUP_BIPREDICTIVE_KHR between
frames encoded with other <<encode-av1-rate-control-group,rate control
groups>> within the <<encode-av1-gop,GOP>>.

items.name: temporalLayerCount
items.text:
pname:temporalLayerCount specifies the number of AV1 temporal layers
that the application intends to use.

items.name: sType

values, for each <<encode-av1-rate-control-group,rate control group>>,
that the implementation's rate control algorithm will use when
pname:useMinQIndex is set to ename:VK_TRUE.

items.name: useMaxQIndex
items.text:
pname:useMaxQIndex indicates whether the quantizer index values
determined by rate control will be clamped to the upper bounds on the
quantizer index values specified in pname:maxQIndex.

items.name: maxQIndex

values, for each <<encode-av1-rate-control-group,rate control group>>,
that the implementation's rate control algorithm will use when
pname:useMaxQIndex is set to ename:VK_TRUE.

items.name: useMaxFrameSize

pname:useMaxFrameSize indicates whether the implementation's rate
control algorithm should: use the values specified in pname:maxFrameSize
as the upper bounds on the encoded frame size for each
<<encode-av1-rate-control-group,rate control group>>.

items.name: maxFrameSize

pname:maxFrameSize specifies the upper bounds on the encoded frame size,
for each <<encode-av1-rate-control-group,rate control group>>, when
pname:useMaxFrameSize is set to ename:VK_TRUE.

items.name: encodeInputPictureGranularity
items.text:
pname:encodeInputPictureGranularity indicates the granularity at which
<<encode-input-picture,encode input picture>> data is encoded and may:
indicate a texel granularity up to the size of the largest supported
codec-specific coding block.
This capability does not impose any valid usage constraints on the
application, however, depending on the contents of the encode input
picture, it may: have effects on the encoded bitstream, as described in
more detail below.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_CAPABILITY_PRECEDING_EXTERNALLY_ENCODED_BYTES_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_CAPABILITY_PRECEDING_EXTERNALLY_ENCODED_BYTES_BIT_KHR
specifies that the implementation supports the use of
slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:precedingExternallyEncodedBytes.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_CAPABILITY_INSUFFICIENT_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_RANGE_DETECTION_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_CAPABILITY_INSUFFICIENT_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_RANGE_DETECTION_BIT_KHR
specifies that the implementation is able to detect and report when the
destination video bitstream buffer range provided by the application is
not sufficiently large to fit the encoded bitstream data produced by a
video encode operation by reporting the
ename:VK_QUERY_RESULT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_RANGE_KHR
<<query-result-status-codes,query result status code>>.
+
[NOTE]
====
Some implementations may: not be able to reliably detect insufficient
bitstream buffer range conditions in all situations.
Such implementations will not report support for the
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_CAPABILITY_INSUFFICIENT_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_RANGE_DETECTION_BIT_KHR
encode capability flag for the video profile, but may: still report the
ename:VK_QUERY_RESULT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_RANGE_KHR query
result status code in certain cases.
Applications should: always check for the specific query result status code
ename:VK_QUERY_RESULT_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_RANGE_KHR even
when this encode capability flag is not supported by the implementation for
the video profile in question.
However, applications must: not assume that a different negative query
result status code indicating an unsuccessful completion of a video encode
operation is not the result of an insufficient bitstream buffer condition
unless this encode capability flag is supported.
====

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_FEEDBACK_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_OFFSET_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_FEEDBACK_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_OFFSET_BIT_KHR specifies
that queries managed by the pool will capture the byte offset of the
bitstream data written by the video encode operation to the bitstream
buffer specified in slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBuffer relative
to the offset specified in
slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBufferOffset.
For the first video encode operation issued by any
<<video-encode-commands,video encode command>>, this value will always
be zero, meaning that bitstream data is always written to the buffer
specified in slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBuffer starting from
the offset specified in
slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBufferOffset.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_FEEDBACK_BITSTREAM_BYTES_WRITTEN_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_FEEDBACK_BITSTREAM_BYTES_WRITTEN_BIT_KHR specifies
that queries managed by the pool will capture the number of bytes
written by the video encode operation to the bitstream buffer specified
in slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBuffer.

items.name: sType
items.text: pname:sType is a elink:VkStructureType value identifying this structure.

items.name: pNext
items.text:
pname:pNext is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this
structure.

items.name: flags
items.text:
pname:flags is a bitmask of elink:VkVideoEncodeH264CapabilityFlagBitsKHR
indicating supported H.264 encoding capabilities.

items.name: maxLevelIdc
items.text:
pname:maxLevelIdc is a code:StdVideoH264LevelIdc value indicating the
maximum H.264 level supported by the profile, where enum constant
`STD_VIDEO_H264_LEVEL_IDC_<major>_<minor>` identifies H.264 level
`<major>.<minor>` as defined in section A.3 of the <<itu-t-h264,ITU-T
H.264 Specification>>.

items.name: maxSliceCount
items.text:
pname:maxSliceCount indicates the maximum number of slices that can: be
encoded for a single picture.
Further restrictions may: apply to the number of slices that can: be
encoded for a single picture depending on other capabilities and
codec-specific rules.

items.name: maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount
items.text:
pname:maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount indicates the maximum number of
reference pictures the implementation supports in the reference list L0
for <<encode-h264-p-pic,P pictures>>.
+
[NOTE]
====
As implementations may: <<encode-overrides,override>> the reference lists,
pname:maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount does not limit the number of elements that
the application can: specify in the L0 reference list for P pictures.
However, if pname:maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount is zero, then the use of P
pictures is not allowed.
====

items.name: maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount
items.text:
pname:maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount indicates the maximum number of
reference pictures the implementation supports in the reference list L0
for <<encode-h264-b-pic,B pictures>>.

items.name: maxL1ReferenceCount
items.text:
pname:maxL1ReferenceCount indicates the maximum number of reference
pictures the implementation supports in the reference list L1 if
encoding of <<encode-h264-b-pic,B pictures>> is supported.
+
[NOTE]
====
As implementations may: <<encode-overrides,override>> the reference lists,
pname:maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount and pname:maxL1ReferenceCount does not
limit the number of elements that the application can: specify in the L0 and
L1 reference lists for B pictures.
However, if pname:maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount and pname:maxL1ReferenceCount
are both zero, then the use of B pictures is not allowed.
====

items.name: maxTemporalLayerCount
items.text:
pname:maxTemporalLayerCount indicates the maximum number of H.264
temporal layers supported by the implementation.

items.name: expectDyadicTemporalLayerPattern
items.text:
pname:expectDyadicTemporalLayerPattern indicates that the
implementation's rate control algorithms expect the application to use a
<<encode-h264-layer-pattern-dyadic,dyadic temporal layer pattern>> when
encoding multiple temporal layers.

items.name: minQp
items.text: pname:minQp indicates the minimum QP value supported.

items.name: maxQp
items.text: pname:maxQp indicates the maximum QP value supported.

items.name: prefersGopRemainingFrames
items.text:
pname:prefersGopRemainingFrames indicates that the implementation's rate
control algorithm prefers the application to specify the number of
frames of each type <<encode-h264-gop-remaining-frames,remaining>> in
the current <<encode-h264-gop,group of pictures>> when beginning a
<<video-coding-scope,video coding scope>>.

items.name: requiresGopRemainingFrames
items.text:
pname:requiresGopRemainingFrames indicates that the implementation's
rate control algorithm requires the application to specify the number of
frames of each type <<encode-h264-gop-remaining-frames,remaining>> in
the current <<encode-h264-gop,group of pictures>> when beginning a
<<video-coding-scope,video coding scope>>.

elink:VkVideoEncodeH264StdFlagBitsKHR indicating capabilities related to
H.264 syntax elements.

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeH264CapabilitiesKHR

pages.desc: H.264 encode capability flags

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_HRD_COMPLIANCE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_HRD_COMPLIANCE_BIT_KHR specifies
whether the implementation may: be able to generate HRD compliant
bitstreams if any of the code:nal_hrd_parameters_present_flag or
code:vcl_hrd_parameters_present_flag members of
code:StdVideoH264SpsVuiFlags are set to `1` in the
<<encode-h264-active-sps,active SPS>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_PREDICTION_WEIGHT_TABLE_GENERATED_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_PREDICTION_WEIGHT_TABLE_GENERATED_BIT_KHR
specifies that if code:StdVideoH264PpsFlags::code:weighted_pred_flag is
set to `1` or
code:StdVideoH264PictureParameterSet::code:weighted_bipred_idc is set to
code:STD_VIDEO_H264_WEIGHTED_BIPRED_IDC_EXPLICIT in the
<<encode-h264-active-pps,active PPS>> when encoding a
<<encode-h264-p-pic,P picture>> or <<encode-h264-b-pic,B picture>>,
respectively, then the implementation is able to internally decide
syntax for code:pred_weight_table, as defined in section 7.4.3.2 of the
<<itu-t-h264,ITU-T H.264 Specification>>, and the application is not
required: to provide a weight table in the
<<encode-h264-slice-header-params,H.264 slice header parameters>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_ROW_UNALIGNED_SLICE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_ROW_UNALIGNED_SLICE_BIT_KHR
specifies that each slice in a frame with multiple slices may begin or
finish at any offset in a macroblock row.
If not supported, all slices in the frame must: begin at the start of a
macroblock row (and hence each slice must: finish at the end of a
macroblock row).
When a picture is encoded with <<encode-intra-refresh,intra refresh>>,
encoding non-rectangular slices also requires: support for the
slink:VkVideoEncodeIntraRefreshCapabilitiesKHR::pname:nonRectangularIntraRefreshRegions
capability.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_DIFFERENT_SLICE_TYPE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_DIFFERENT_SLICE_TYPE_BIT_KHR
specifies that when a frame is encoded with multiple slices, the
implementation allows encoding each slice with a different
code:StdVideoEncodeH264SliceHeader::code:slice_type specified in the
<<encode-h264-slice-header-params,H.264 slice header parameters>>.
If not supported, all slices of the frame must: be encoded with the same
code:slice_type which corresponds to the picture type of the frame.
There is one exception to this rule: if the picture is encoded with the
<<encode-intra-refresh-modes,intra refresh mode>>
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_PER_PICTURE_PARTITION_BIT_KHR,
then the currently refreshed slice must: specify the code:slice_type
code:STD_VIDEO_H264_SLICE_TYPE_I and can: differ from the
code:slice_type of the other slices regardless of whether
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_DIFFERENT_SLICE_TYPE_BIT_KHR is
supported.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L0_LIST_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L0_LIST_BIT_KHR
specifies support for using a <<encode-h264-b-pic,B frame>> as L0
reference, as specified in
code:StdVideoEncodeH264ReferenceListsInfo::code:RefPicList0 in the
<<encode-h264-picture-info,H.264 picture information>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L1_LIST_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L1_LIST_BIT_KHR
specifies support for using a <<encode-h264-b-pic,B frame>> as L1
reference, as specified in
code:StdVideoEncodeH264ReferenceListsInfo::code:RefPicList1 in the
<<encode-h264-picture-info,H.264 picture information>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_PER_PICTURE_TYPE_MIN_MAX_QP_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_PER_PICTURE_TYPE_MIN_MAX_QP_BIT_KHR
specifies support for specifying different QP values in the members of
slink:VkVideoEncodeH264QpKHR.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_PER_SLICE_CONSTANT_QP_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_PER_SLICE_CONSTANT_QP_BIT_KHR
specifies support for specifying different constant QP values for each
slice.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_GENERATE_PREFIX_NALU_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_GENERATE_PREFIX_NALU_BIT_KHR
specifies support for generating prefix NAL units by setting
slink:VkVideoEncodeH264PictureInfoKHR::pname:generatePrefixNalu to
ename:VK_TRUE.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_MB_QP_DIFF_WRAPAROUND_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_MB_QP_DIFF_WRAPAROUND_BIT_KHR
specifies support for wraparound during the calculation of the QP values
of subsequently encoded macroblocks, as defined in equation 7-37 of the
<<itu-t-h264,ITU-T H.264 Specification>>.
If not supported, equation 7-37 of the <<itu-t-h264,ITU-T H.264
Specification>> is effectively reduced to the following:
+
[eq]#QP~Y~ = QP~Y,PREV~ {plus} code:mb_qp_delta#
+
[NOTE]
====
The effect of this is that the maximum QP difference across subsequent
macroblocks is limited to the [eq]#[-(26 {plus} QpBdOffset~Y~ / 2), 25
{plus} QpBdOffset~Y~ / 2]# range.
====

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_B_PICTURE_INTRA_REFRESH_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_CAPABILITY_B_PICTURE_INTRA_REFRESH_BIT_KHR
specifies support for encoding <<encode-h264-b-pic,B pictures>> with
<<encode-intra-refresh,intra refresh>> enabled.

items.name: generatePrefixNalu

pname:generatePrefixNalu controls whether prefix NALUs are generated
before slice NALUs into the target bitstream, as defined in sections
7.3.2.12 and 7.4.2.12 of the <<itu-t-h264,ITU-T H.264 Specification>>.

items.name: pStdSliceHeader

bitstream, as defined in annex C of the <<itu-t-h264,ITU-T H.264

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_RATE_CONTROL_REGULAR_GOP_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_RATE_CONTROL_REGULAR_GOP_BIT_KHR specifies
that the application intends to use a <<encode-h264-regular-gop, regular
GOP structure>> according to the parameters specified in the
pname:gopFrameCount, pname:idrPeriod, and pname:consecutiveBFrameCount
members of the slink:VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlInfoKHR structure.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H264_RATE_CONTROL_REFERENCE_PATTERN_FLAT_BIT_KHR

<<encode-h264-ref-pattern-flat,flat reference pattern>> in the GOP.

<<encode-h264-ref-pattern-dyadic,dyadic reference pattern>> in the GOP.

items.text:

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlFlagBitsKHR

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlFlagsKHR

pages.desc: Structure describing H.264 stream rate control parameters

items.name: sType
items.text: pname:sType is a elink:VkStructureType value identifying this structure.

items.name: pNext
items.text:
pname:pNext is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this
structure.

items.name: flags
items.text:
pname:flags is a bitmask of
elink:VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlFlagBitsKHR specifying H.264 rate
control flags.

items.name: gopFrameCount
items.text:
pname:gopFrameCount is the number of frames within a <<encode-h264-gop,
group of pictures (GOP)>> intended to be used by the application.
If it is 0, the rate control algorithm may: assume an
implementation-dependent GOP length.
If it is code:UINT32_MAX, the GOP length is treated as infinite.

items.name: idrPeriod
items.text:
pname:idrPeriod is the interval, in terms of number of frames, between
two <<encode-h264-idr-pic,IDR frames>> (see <<encode-h264-idr-period,IDR
period>>).
If it is 0, the rate control algorithm may: assume an
implementation-dependent IDR period.
If it is code:UINT32_MAX, the IDR period is treated as infinite.

items.name: consecutiveBFrameCount
items.text:
pname:consecutiveBFrameCount is the number of consecutive B frames
between I and/or P frames within the <<encode-h264-gop,GOP>>.

items.name: temporalLayerCount
items.text:
pname:temporalLayerCount specifies the number of H.264 temporal layers
that the application intends to use.

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlInfoKHR

pages.desc: Structure describing H.264 per-layer rate control parameters

items.name: sType
items.text: pname:sType is a elink:VkStructureType value identifying this structure.

items.name: pNext
items.text:
pname:pNext is `NULL` or a pointer to a structure extending this
structure.

items.name: useMinQp
items.text:
pname:useMinQp indicates whether the QP values determined by rate
control will be clamped to the lower bounds on the QP values specified
in pname:minQp.

items.name: minQp
items.text:
pname:minQp specifies the lower bounds on the QP values, for each
picture type, that the implementation's rate control algorithm will use
when pname:useMinQp is ename:VK_TRUE.

items.name: useMaxQp
items.text:
pname:useMaxQp indicates whether the QP values determined by rate
control will be clamped to the upper bounds on the QP values specified
in pname:maxQp.

items.name: maxQp
items.text:
pname:maxQp specifies the upper bounds on the QP values, for each
picture type, that the implementation's rate control algorithm will use
when pname:useMaxQp is ename:VK_TRUE.

items.name: useMaxFrameSize
items.text:
pname:useMaxFrameSize indicates whether the implementation's rate
control algorithm should: use the values specified in pname:maxFrameSize
as the upper bounds on the encoded frame size for each picture type.

items.name: maxFrameSize
items.text:
pname:maxFrameSize specifies the upper bounds on the encoded frame size,
for each picture type, when pname:useMaxFrameSize is ename:VK_TRUE.

items.text:
pname:useMaxLevelIdc indicates whether the value of pname:maxLevelIdc
should be used by the implementation.

pname:maxLevelIdc and uses the value of
slink:VkVideoEncodeH264CapabilitiesKHR::pname:maxLevelIdc, as reported
by flink:vkGetPhysicalDeviceVideoCapabilitiesKHR for the video profile.

pname:maxLevelIdc is a code:StdVideoH264LevelIdc value specifying the
upper bound on the H.264 level for the video bitstreams produced by the
created video session, where enum constant
`STD_VIDEO_H264_LEVEL_IDC_<major>_<minor>` identifies H.264 level
`<major>.<minor>` as defined in section A.3 of the <<itu-t-h264,ITU-T
H.264 Specification>>.
