`STD_VIDEO_H265_LEVEL_IDC_<major>_<minor>` identifies H.265 level
`<major>.<minor>` as defined in section A.4 of the <<itu-t-h265,ITU-T
H.265 Specification>>.

items.name: maxSliceSegmentCount
items.text:
pname:maxSliceSegmentCount indicates the maximum number of slice
segments that can: be encoded for a single picture.
Further restrictions may: apply to the number of slice segments that
can: be encoded for a single picture depending on other capabilities and
codec-specific rules.

items.name: maxTiles
items.text:
pname:maxTiles indicates the maximum number of H.265 tile columns and
rows, as defined in sections 3.175 and 3.176 of the <<itu-t-h265,ITU-T
H.265 Specification>> that can: be encoded for a single picture.
Further restrictions may: apply to the number of H.265 tiles that can:
be encoded for a single picture depending on other capabilities and
codec-specific rules.

items.name: ctbSizes
items.text:
pname:ctbSizes is a bitmask of elink:VkVideoEncodeH265CtbSizeFlagBitsKHR
describing the supported CTB sizes.

items.name: transformBlockSizes
items.text:
pname:transformBlockSizes is a bitmask of
elink:VkVideoEncodeH265TransformBlockSizeFlagBitsKHR describing the
supported transform block sizes.

items.name: maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount
items.text:
pname:maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount indicates the maximum number of
reference pictures the implementation supports in the reference list L0
for <<encode-h265-p-pic,P pictures>>.
+
[NOTE]
====
As implementations may: <<encode-overrides,override>> the reference lists,
pname:maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount does not limit the number of elements that
the application can: specify in the L0 reference list for P pictures.
However, if pname:maxPPictureL0ReferenceCount is zero, then the use of P
pictures is not allowed.
In case of H.265 encoding, pictures can: be encoded using only forward
prediction even if P pictures are not supported, as the <<itu-t-h265,ITU-T
H.265 Specification>> supports _generalized P & B frames_ (also known as low
delay B frames) whereas B frames can: refer to past frames through both the
L0 and L1 reference lists.
====

items.name: maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount
items.text:
pname:maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount indicates the maximum number of
reference pictures the implementation supports in the reference list L0
for <<encode-h265-b-pic,B pictures>>.

items.name: maxL1ReferenceCount
items.text:
pname:maxL1ReferenceCount indicates the maximum number of reference
pictures the implementation supports in the reference list L1 if
encoding of <<encode-h265-b-pic,B pictures>> is supported.
+
[NOTE]
====
As implementations may: <<encode-overrides,override>> the reference lists,
pname:maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount and pname:maxL1ReferenceCount does not
limit the number of elements that the application can: specify in the L0 and
L1 reference lists for B pictures.
However, if pname:maxBPictureL0ReferenceCount and pname:maxL1ReferenceCount
are both zero, then the use of B pictures is not allowed.
====

items.name: maxSubLayerCount
items.text:
pname:maxSubLayerCount indicates the maximum number of H.265 sub-layers
supported by the implementation.

items.name: expectDyadicTemporalSubLayerPattern
items.text:
pname:expectDyadicTemporalSubLayerPattern indicates that the
implementation's rate control algorithms expect the application to use a
<<encode-h265-layer-pattern-dyadic,dyadic temporal sub-layer pattern>>
when encoding multiple temporal sub-layers.

items.name: minQp
items.text: pname:minQp indicates the minimum QP value supported.

items.name: maxQp
items.text: pname:maxQp indicates the maximum QP value supported.

items.name: prefersGopRemainingFrames
items.text:
pname:prefersGopRemainingFrames indicates that the implementation's rate
control algorithm prefers the application to specify the number of
frames of each type <<encode-h265-gop-remaining-frames,remaining>> in
the current <<encode-h265-gop,group of pictures>> when beginning a
<<video-coding-scope,video coding scope>>.

items.name: requiresGopRemainingFrames
items.text:
pname:requiresGopRemainingFrames indicates that the implementation's
rate control algorithm requires the application to specify the number of
frames of each type <<encode-h265-gop-remaining-frames,remaining>> in
the current <<encode-h265-gop,group of pictures>> when beginning a
<<video-coding-scope,video coding scope>>.

items.name: stdSyntaxFlags
items.text:
pname:stdSyntaxFlags is a bitmask of
elink:VkVideoEncodeH265StdFlagBitsKHR indicating capabilities related to
H.265 syntax elements.

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeH265CapabilitiesKHR

pages.desc: Video encode H.265 capability flags

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_HRD_COMPLIANCE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_HRD_COMPLIANCE_BIT_KHR specifies
whether the implementation may: be able to generate HRD compliant
bitstreams if any of the code:nal_hrd_parameters_present_flag,
code:vcl_hrd_parameters_present_flag, or
code:sub_pic_hrd_params_present_flag members of
code:StdVideoH265HrdFlags are set to `1` in the HRD parameters of the
<<encode-h265-active-vps,active VPS>> or <<encode-h265-active-sps,active
SPS>>, or if
code:StdVideoH265SpsVuiFlags::code:vui_hrd_parameters_present_flag is
set to `1` in the <<encode-h265-active-sps,active SPS>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_PREDICTION_WEIGHT_TABLE_GENERATED_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_PREDICTION_WEIGHT_TABLE_GENERATED_BIT_KHR
specifies that if the code:weighted_pred_flag or the
code:weighted_bipred_flag member of code:StdVideoH265PpsFlags is set to
`1` in the <<encode-h265-active-pps,active PPS>> when encoding a
<<encode-h265-p-pic,P picture>> or <<encode-h265-b-pic,B picture>>,
respectively, then the implementation is able to internally decide
syntax for code:pred_weight_table, as defined in section 7.4.7.3 of the
<<itu-t-h265,ITU-T H.265 Specification>>, and the application is not
required: to provide a weight table in the
<<encode-h265-slice-segment-header-params,H.265 slice segment header
parameters>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_ROW_UNALIGNED_SLICE_SEGMENT_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_ROW_UNALIGNED_SLICE_SEGMENT_BIT_KHR
specifies that each slice segment in a frame with a single or multiple
tiles per slice may begin or finish at any offset in a CTB row.
If not supported, all slice segments in such a frame must: begin at the
start of a CTB row (and hence each slice segment must: finish at the end
of a CTB row).
Also indicates that each slice segment in a frame with multiple slices
per tile may begin or finish at any offset within the enclosing tile's
CTB row.
If not supported, slice segments in such a frame must: begin at the
start of the enclosing tile's CTB row (and hence each slice segment
must: finish at the end of the enclosing tile's CTB row).
When a picture is encoded with <<encode-intra-refresh,intra refresh>>,
encoding non-rectangular slice segments also requires: support for the
slink:VkVideoEncodeIntraRefreshCapabilitiesKHR::pname:nonRectangularIntraRefreshRegions
capability.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_DIFFERENT_SLICE_SEGMENT_TYPE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_DIFFERENT_SLICE_SEGMENT_TYPE_BIT_KHR
specifies that when a frame is encoded with multiple slice segments, the
implementation allows encoding each slice segment with a different
code:StdVideoEncodeH265SliceSegmentHeader::code:slice_type specified in
the <<encode-h265-slice-segment-header-params,H.265 slice segment header
parameters>>.
If not supported, all slice segments of the frame must: be encoded with
the same code:slice_type which corresponds to the picture type of the
frame.
There is one exception to this rule: if the picture is encoded with the
<<encode-intra-refresh-modes,intra refresh mode>>
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_PER_PICTURE_PARTITION_BIT_KHR,
then the currently refreshed slice segment must: specify the
code:slice_type code:STD_VIDEO_H265_SLICE_TYPE_I and can: differ from
the code:slice_type of the other slice segments regardless of whether
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_DIFFERENT_SLICE_SEGMENT_TYPE_BIT_KHR
is supported.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L0_LIST_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L0_LIST_BIT_KHR
specifies support for using a <<encode-h265-b-pic,B frame>> as L0
reference, as specified in
code:StdVideoEncodeH265ReferenceListsInfo::code:RefPicList0 in the
<<encode-h265-picture-info,H.265 picture information>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L1_LIST_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_B_FRAME_IN_L1_LIST_BIT_KHR
specifies support for using a <<encode-h265-b-pic,B frame>> as L1
reference, as specified in
code:StdVideoEncodeH265ReferenceListsInfo::code:RefPicList1 in the
<<encode-h265-picture-info,H.265 picture information>>.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_PER_PICTURE_TYPE_MIN_MAX_QP_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_PER_PICTURE_TYPE_MIN_MAX_QP_BIT_KHR
specifies support for specifying different QP values in the members of
slink:VkVideoEncodeH265QpKHR.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_PER_SLICE_SEGMENT_CONSTANT_QP_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_PER_SLICE_SEGMENT_CONSTANT_QP_BIT_KHR
specifies support for specifying different constant QP values for each
slice segment.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_MULTIPLE_TILES_PER_SLICE_SEGMENT_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_MULTIPLE_TILES_PER_SLICE_SEGMENT_BIT_KHR
specifies whether encoding multiple tiles per slice segment, as defined
in section 6.3.1 of the <<itu-t-h265,ITU-T H.265 Specification>>, is
supported.
If this capability flag is not present, then the implementation is only
able to encode a single tile for each slice segment.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_MULTIPLE_SLICE_SEGMENTS_PER_TILE_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_MULTIPLE_SLICE_SEGMENTS_PER_TILE_BIT_KHR
specifies whether encoding multiple slice segments per tile, as defined
in section 6.3.1 of the <<itu-t-h265,ITU-T H.265 Specification>>, is
supported.
If this capability flag is not present, then the implementation is only
able to encode a single slice segment for each tile.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_CU_QP_DIFF_WRAPAROUND_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_CU_QP_DIFF_WRAPAROUND_BIT_KHR
indicates support for wraparound during the calculation of the QP values
of subsequently encoded coding units, as defined in section 7.4.9.14 of
the <<itu-t-h265,ITU-T H.265 Specification>>.
If not supported, equation 8-283 of the <<itu-t-h265,ITU-T H.265
Specification>> is effectively reduced to the following:
+
[eq]#Qp~Y~ = qP~Y_PRED~ {plus} code:CuQpDeltaVal#
+
[NOTE]
====
The effect of this is that the maximum QP difference across subsequent
coding units is limited to the [eq]#[-(26 {plus} QpBdOffset~Y~ / 2), 25
{plus} QpBdOffset~Y~ / 2]# range.
====

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_B_PICTURE_INTRA_REFRESH_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_CAPABILITY_B_PICTURE_INTRA_REFRESH_BIT_KHR
specifies support for encoding <<encode-h265-b-pic,B pictures>> with
<<encode-intra-refresh,intra refresh>> enabled.

structure.

group of pictures (GOP)>> intended to be used by the application.
If it is 0, the rate control algorithm may: assume an
implementation-dependent GOP length.
If it is code:UINT32_MAX, the GOP length is treated as infinite.

two <<encode-h265-idr-pic,IDR frames>> (see <<encode-h265-idr-period,IDR
period>>).
If it is 0, the rate control algorithm may: assume an
implementation-dependent IDR period.
If it is code:UINT32_MAX, the IDR period is treated as infinite.

items.name: consecutiveBFrameCount

between I and/or P frames within the <<encode-h265-gop,GOP>>.

application intends to use.

<<encode-intra-refresh-cycle-duration,intra refresh cycle duration>>.

items.name: maxIntraRefreshActiveReferencePictures
items.text:
pname:maxIntraRefreshActiveReferencePictures is the maximum number of
<<active-reference-pictures,active reference pictures>> when encoding
pictures with <<encode-intra-refresh,intra refresh>> enabled.
This capability indicates additional restrictions beyond the maximum
number of <<active-reference-pictures,active reference pictures>>
supported by the video profile, as reported in
slink:VkVideoCapabilitiesKHR::pname:maxActiveReferencePictures and the
maximum requested at video session creation time in
slink:VkVideoSessionCreateInfoKHR::pname:maxActiveReferencePictures.

items.name: partitionIndependentIntraRefreshRegions
items.text:
pname:partitionIndependentIntraRefreshRegions specifies whether the
implementation supports intra refresh regions that are independent of
the picture partitioning used during encoding.
If it is ename:VK_TRUE, then pictures can: be encoded with multiple
picture partitions, independent of the used intra refresh mode.
Otherwise, pictures cannot: be encoded with multiple picture partitions
with any intra refresh mode other than
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_PER_PICTURE_PARTITION_BIT_KHR.
+
[NOTE]
====
This capability is only indicative for <<encode-av1-profile,AV1 encode
profiles>> and does not impose any restrictions on the application as
implementations may change the application requested picture partitioning
according to implementation-specific restrictions.
====

items.name: nonRectangularIntraRefreshRegions
items.text:
pname:nonRectangularIntraRefreshRegions specifies whether the
implementation supports non-rectangular intra refresh regions.
+
[NOTE]
====
If this capability is not supported, then using per picture partition intra
refresh may impose additional restrictions on the number of picture
partitions a picture can be encoded with.
====

pages.name: VkVideoEncodeIntraRefreshInfoKHR

pages.desc: Video encode intra refresh modes

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_NONE_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_NONE_KHR specifies that intra
refresh must: not be used.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_PER_PICTURE_PARTITION_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_PER_PICTURE_PARTITION_BIT_KHR
specifies the use of _per picture partition intra refresh_.
In this mode each intra refresh region [eq]#i# corresponds to the
encoded picture partition [eq]#i#.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_BLOCK_BASED_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_BLOCK_BASED_BIT_KHR specifies
the use of any _block-based intra refresh_.
In this mode each intra refresh region encompasses a set of coding
blocks, independent of encoded picture partitions but without any
additional guarantees on the granularity at which the picture is split
into intra refresh regions.
When using this mode, the set of coding blocks comprising the intra
refresh regions and the direction of intra refresh are
implementation-defined.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_BLOCK_ROW_BASED_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_BLOCK_ROW_BASED_BIT_KHR
specifies the use of _block-row-based intra refresh_.
This mode is a block-based intra refresh mode where each intra refresh
region encompasses a set of coding block rows.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_BLOCK_COLUMN_BASED_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_INTRA_REFRESH_MODE_BLOCK_COLUMN_BASED_BIT_KHR
specifies the use of _block-column-based intra refresh_.
This mode is a block-based intra refresh mode where each intra refresh
region encompasses a set of coding block columns.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_PER_PARTITION_FEEDBACK_STATUS_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_PER_PARTITION_FEEDBACK_STATUS_BIT_KHR specifies
that queries managed by the pool will capture the result status of each
encoded picture partition.
These result status values are reported as elink:VkQueryResultStatusKHR
values, similar to <<queries-result-status-only,result status queries>>
but indicate the result status of the encoding of individual picture
partitions instead of that of the whole video encode operation.

items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_PER_PARTITION_FEEDBACK_BITSTREAM_BUFFER_OFFSET_BIT_KHR
specifies that queries managed by the pool will capture the byte offset
of the bitstream data of the corresponding picture partition written to
the bitstream buffer specified in
slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBuffer relative to the offset
specified in slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBufferOffset.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_PER_PARTITION_FEEDBACK_BITSTREAM_BYTES_WRITTEN_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_PER_PARTITION_FEEDBACK_BITSTREAM_BYTES_WRITTEN_BIT_KHR
specifies that queries managed by the pool will capture the number of
bytes written by the video encode operation for the corresponding
picture partition to the bitstream buffer specified in
slink:VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR::pname:dstBuffer.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_DEFAULT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_DEFAULT_KHR specifies the use of
implementation-specific rate control.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_DISABLED_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_DISABLED_BIT_KHR specifies that
rate control is disabled and the application will specify per-operation
rate control parameters controlling the encoding quality.
In this mode implementations will encode pictures independently of the
output bitrate of prior video encode operations.
** When using an <<encode-h264-profile,H.264 encode profile>>,
implementations will use the QP value specified in
slink:VkVideoEncodeH264NaluSliceInfoKHR::pname:constantQp to control
the quality of the encoded picture.
** When using an <<encode-h265-profile,H.265 encode profile>>,
implementations will use the QP value specified in
slink:VkVideoEncodeH265NaluSliceSegmentInfoKHR::pname:constantQp to
control the quality of the encoded picture.
** When using an <<encode-av1-profile,AV1 encode profile>>,
implementations will use the quantizer index value specified in
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1PictureInfoKHR::pname:constantQIndex to control
the quality of the encoded picture.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_CBR_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_CBR_BIT_KHR specifies the use of
constant bitrate (CBR) rate control mode.
In this mode the implementation will attempt to produce the encoded
bitstream at a constant bitrate while conforming to the constraints of
other rate control parameters.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_VBR_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_MODE_VBR_BIT_KHR specifies the use of
variable bitrate (VBR) rate control mode.
In this mode the implementation will produce the encoded bitstream at a
variable bitrate according to the constraints of other rate control
parameters.

pages.desc: Range compression operation to perform for encode rgb conversion

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RGB_RANGE_COMPRESSION_FULL_RANGE_BIT_VALVE
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RGB_RANGE_COMPRESSION_FULL_RANGE_BIT_VALVE
specifies the following transformations are applied:
+
[latexmath]
++++
\begin{aligned}
Y' &= C'_{rgba}[G] \\
C_B &= C'_{rgba}[B] - {{2^{(n-1)}}\over{(2^n) - 1}} \\
C_R &= C'_{rgba}[R] - {{2^{(n-1)}}\over{(2^n) - 1}}
\end{aligned}
++++
+
[NOTE]
====
These formulae correspond to the "`full range`" encoding in the
"`Quantization schemes`" chapter of the <<data-format,Khronos Data Format
Specification>>.

Should any future amendments be made to the ITU specifications from which
these equations are derived, the formulae used by Vulkan may: also be
updated to maintain parity.
====

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RGB_RANGE_COMPRESSION_NARROW_RANGE_BIT_VALVE
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_RGB_RANGE_COMPRESSION_NARROW_RANGE_BIT_VALVE
specifies the following transformations are applied:
+
[latexmath]
++++
\begin{aligned}
Y' &= {{C'_{rgba}[G] \times (2^n-1) - 16\times 2^{n-8}}\over{219\times 2^{n-8}}} \\
C_B &= {{C'_{rgba}[B] \times \left(2^n-1\right) - 128\times 2^{n-8}}\over{224\times 2^{n-8}}} \\
C_R &= {{C'_{rgba}[R] \times \left(2^n-1\right) - 128\times 2^{n-8}}\over{224\times 2^{n-8}}}
\end{aligned}
++++
+
[NOTE]
====
These formulae correspond to the "`narrow range`" encoding in the
"`Quantization schemes`" chapter of the <<data-format,Khronos Data Format
Specification>>.

Unlike <<textures-sampler-YCbCr-conversion-rangeexpand, sampler {YCbCr}
range expansion>>, no precision guarantees are made for video encode
{RGBprime} range compression.
====

pages.desc: Video encode tuning mode

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_DEFAULT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_DEFAULT_KHR specifies the default
tuning mode.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_HIGH_QUALITY_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_HIGH_QUALITY_KHR specifies that video
encoding is tuned for high quality.
When using this tuning mode, the implementation may: compromise the
latency of video encoding operations to improve quality.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_LOW_LATENCY_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_LOW_LATENCY_KHR specifies that video
encoding is tuned for low latency.
When using this tuning mode, the implementation may: compromise quality
to increase the performance and lower the latency of video encode
operations.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_ULTRA_LOW_LATENCY_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_ULTRA_LOW_LATENCY_KHR specifies that
video encoding is tuned for ultra-low latency.
When using this tuning mode, the implementation may: compromise quality
to maximize the performance and minimize the latency of video encoding
operations.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_LOSSLESS_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_TUNING_MODE_LOSSLESS_KHR specifies that video
encoding is tuned for lossless encoding.
When using this tuning mode, video encode operations produce lossless
output.

items.name: VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_USAGE_STREAMING_BIT_KHR

items.name: compatibleSuperblockSizes
items.text:
pname:compatibleSuperblockSizes is a bitmask of
elink:VkVideoEncodeAV1SuperblockSizeFlagBitsKHR indicating the AV1
superblock sizes that quantization maps using this video format are
compatible with.
+
[NOTE]
====
The value of pname:compatibleSuperblockSizes does not limit the use of the
specific quantization map format, but does limit the implementation in being
able to encode pictures with superblock sizes not included in
pname:compatibleSuperblockSizes but otherwise supported by the used video
profile, as indicated by
slink:VkVideoEncodeAV1CapabilitiesKHR::pname:superblockSizes.
In particular, using smaller
<<encode-quantization-map-texel-size,quantization map texel sizes>> may
prevent implementations from encoding with larger superblock sizes which may
have a negative impact on the efficiency of the encoder.
====

items.name: VK_VIDEO_SESSION_CREATE_ALLOW_ENCODE_PARAMETER_OPTIMIZATIONS_BIT_KHR
items.text:
ename:VK_VIDEO_SESSION_CREATE_ALLOW_ENCODE_PARAMETER_OPTIMIZATIONS_BIT_KHR
specifies that the implementation is allowed to
<<encode-overrides,override>> video session parameters and other
codec-specific encoding parameters to optimize video encode operations
based on the use case information specified in the
<<video-profiles,video profile>> and the used
<<encode-quality-level,video encode quality level>>.
+
[NOTE]
====
Not specifying
ename:VK_VIDEO_SESSION_CREATE_ALLOW_ENCODE_PARAMETER_OPTIMIZATIONS_BIT_KHR
does not guarantee that the implementation will not do any codec-specific
parameter overrides, as certain overrides are necessary for the correct
operation of the video encoder implementation due to limitations to the
available encoding tools on that implementation.
This flag, however, enables the implementation to apply further optimizing
overrides.
====

items.name: dstArrayElement
items.text:
pname:dstArrayElement is the starting element in that array.
If the descriptor binding identified by pname:dstSet and
pname:dstBinding has a descriptor type of
ename:VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_INLINE_UNIFORM_BLOCK then pname:dstArrayElement
specifies the starting byte offset within the binding.

items.name: descriptorCount
items.text:
pname:descriptorCount is the number of descriptors to update.
If the descriptor binding identified by pname:dstSet and
pname:dstBinding has a descriptor type of
ename:VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_INLINE_UNIFORM_BLOCK, then
pname:descriptorCount specifies the number of bytes to update.
Otherwise,
pname:descriptorCount is one of
** the number of elements in pname:pImageInfo
** the number of elements in pname:pBufferInfo
** the number of elements in pname:pTexelBufferView
** a value matching the pname:dataSize member of a
slink:VkWriteDescriptorSetInlineUniformBlock structure in the
pname:pNext chain
** a value matching the pname:accelerationStructureCount of a
slink:VkWriteDescriptorSetAccelerationStructureKHR
or
slink:VkWriteDescriptorSetAccelerationStructureNV
structure in the pname:pNext chain
** a value matching the pname:descriptorCount of a
slink:VkWriteDescriptorSetTensorARM structure in the pname:pNext chain

items.name: descriptorType
items.text:
pname:descriptorType is a elink:VkDescriptorType specifying the type of
each descriptor in pname:pImageInfo, pname:pBufferInfo, or
pname:pTexelBufferView, as described below.
If sname:VkDescriptorSetLayoutBinding for pname:dstSet at
pname:dstBinding is not equal to ename:VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_MUTABLE_EXT,
pname:descriptorType must:
be the same type as the pname:descriptorType specified in
sname:VkDescriptorSetLayoutBinding for pname:dstSet at pname:dstBinding.
The type of the descriptor also controls which array the descriptors are
taken from.

items.name: pImageInfo
items.text:
pname:pImageInfo is a pointer to an array of slink:VkDescriptorImageInfo
structures or is ignored, as described below.

items.name: pBufferInfo
items.text:
pname:pBufferInfo is a pointer to an array of
slink:VkDescriptorBufferInfo structures or is ignored, as described
below.

If the byte offset stored to the counter buffer location was done using
flink:vkCmdEndTransformFeedbackEXT it can be used to resume transform
feedback from the previous location.
In that case, a pipeline barrier is required between the calls to
fname:vkCmdEndTransformFeedbackEXT and
fname:vkCmdBeginTransformFeedbackEXT, with
ename:VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BIT_EXT as the source and
destination stages,
ename:VK_ACCESS_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_COUNTER_WRITE_BIT_EXT as the source
access and ename:VK_ACCESS_TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_COUNTER_READ_BIT_EXT as
the destination access.
If pname:pCounterBuffers is `NULL`, then transform feedback will start
capturing vertex data to byte offset zero in all bound transform
feedback buffers.
For each element of pname:pCounterBuffers that is dlink:VK_NULL_HANDLE,
transform feedback will start capturing vertex data to byte zero in the
corresponding bound transform feedback buffer.

items.name: pCounterBufferOffsets
items.text:
pname:pCounterBufferOffsets is `NULL` or a pointer to an array of
basetype:VkDeviceSize values specifying offsets within each of the
pname:pCounterBuffers where the counter values were previously written.
The location in each counter buffer at these offsets must: be large
enough to contain 4 bytes of data.
This data is the number of bytes captured by the previous transform
feedback to this buffer.
If pname:pCounterBufferOffsets is `NULL`, then it is assumed the offsets
are zero.

pages.desc: Make transform feedback inactive in the command buffer

items.name: commandBuffer
items.text:
pname:commandBuffer is the command buffer into which the command is
recorded.

items.name: firstCounterBuffer
items.text:
pname:firstCounterBuffer is the index of the first transform feedback
buffer corresponding to pname:pCounterBuffers[0] and
pname:pCounterBufferOffsets[0].

items.name: counterBufferCount
items.text:
pname:counterBufferCount is the size of the pname:pCounterBuffers and
pname:pCounterBufferOffsets arrays.

items.name: pCounterBuffers
items.text:
pname:pCounterBuffers is `NULL` or a pointer to an array of
slink:VkBuffer handles to counter buffers.
The counter buffers are used to record the current byte positions of
each transform feedback buffer where the next vertex output data would
be captured.
This can: be used by a subsequent flink:vkCmdBeginTransformFeedbackEXT
call to resume transform feedback capture from this position.
It can also be used by flink:vkCmdDrawIndirectByteCountEXT to determine
the vertex count of the draw call.

items.name: pCounterBufferOffsets
items.text:
pname:pCounterBufferOffsets is `NULL` or a pointer to an array of
basetype:VkDeviceSize values specifying offsets within each of the
pname:pCounterBuffers where the counter values can be written.
The location in each counter buffer at these offsets must: be large
enough to contain 4 bytes of data.
The data stored at this location is the byte offset from the start of
the transform feedback buffer binding where the next vertex data would
be written.
If pname:pCounterBufferOffsets is `NULL`, then it is assumed the offsets
are zero.
